programme.displayName: Amazon API Gateway Secure REST and HTTP APIs Follow Along
programme.subtitle: Build Lambda-backed APIs with Amazon Cognito authorization, REST API usage plans, and deliberate CORS policies
programme.description: Create two small public API front doors without creating a VPC: a REST API that uses a Cognito user-pool authorizer plus an API key and usage plan, and an HTTP API that uses a JWT authorizer. Both APIs invoke the same Lambda function. The exercise uses a fixed trusted browser origin, https://example.com, to demonstrate restrictive CORS configuration rather than permissive wildcard production defaults.
programme.learningOutcome: Construct secure REST and HTTP APIs with Lambda integrations, Cognito authorizers, usage plans, and CORS controls.

tasks.title: Create and verify temporary training access
tasks.goal: Using an existing non-root administrator, create fa-api-gateway-lab-user, attach AdministratorAccess only for this disposable lab, create one access key, configure the fa-api-gateway-lab CLI profile, and verify the caller.
tasks.whyItMatters: The root user must not be used for ordinary lab work. AdministratorAccess is deliberately broad for a short-lived beginner lab and must be detached before the user is deleted.

consoleSteps.title: Establish the administrator starting point
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in to AWS as an existing non-root administrator. If the account has no administrator, stop and have the account owner create one; do not create root access keys.

instructions.text: Sign in to AWS as an existing non-root administrator. If the account has no administrator, stop and have the account owner create one; do not create root access keys.
In the console header, choose the Region selector and select Europe (London), eu-west-2. IAM is global, but later resources use this Region.
Open IAM from the Services menu.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: You are signed in as an administrator and are at the IAM Create user page.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use root access keys or share root credentials.

consoleSteps.title: Create the console and CLI lab identity

instructions.text: Select Provide user access to the AWS Management Console, select I want to create an IAM user, select Custom password, enter a new temporary password, and select Users must create a new password at next sign-in.
Choose Next, select Attach policies directly, select AdministratorAccess, choose Next, and choose Create user.
Open the created user and record the displayed IAM-user sign-in URL. This is the URL used to sign in as the lab user.
Choose Security credentials, choose Create access key, select Command Line Interface (CLI), select the acknowledgement checkbox, and choose Create access key.
Record the displayed access-key ID as [LAB_ACCESS_KEY_ID]. Copy the secret access key only into the local AWS CLI prompt in the next step; it is shown once.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-api-gateway-lab-user exists, AdministratorAccess is attached, [LAB_ACCESS_KEY_ID] exists for that user, and the IAM-user sign-in URL is recorded.
consoleSteps.warning: Never put the secret access key in notes, screenshots, code, a command, or source control.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-user --user-name fa-api-gateway-lab-user --profile <ADMIN_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: <ADMIN_PROFILE> is the name of a pre-existing local AWS CLI profile whose caller is an account administrator. IAM is global, so no --region is used.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output contains UserName fa-api-gateway-lab-user.
cliSteps.warning: Stop if <ADMIN_PROFILE> is not an administrator profile.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-user-policy --user-name fa-api-gateway-lab-user --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess --profile <ADMIN_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the temporary AWS managed AdministratorAccess policy to only fa-api-gateway-lab-user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes without an error.
cliSteps.warning: This attachment is removed during final cleanup.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-access-key --user-name fa-api-gateway-lab-user --profile <ADMIN_PROFILE>
cliSteps.explanation: Record AccessKey.AccessKeyId as [LAB_ACCESS_KEY_ID]. Copy SecretAccessKey directly to the next interactive command; do not save it in this guide.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response has AccessKeyId and one-time SecretAccessKey fields.
cliSteps.warning: Do not continue if you did not securely capture the secret access key.

cliSteps.command: aws configure --profile fa-api-gateway-lab
cliSteps.explanation: At the prompts enter the newly created access key ID, its secret access key, eu-west-2 for Default Region, and json for Default output format.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The local profile fa-api-gateway-lab is saved.
cliSteps.warning: The command writes credentials to the local AWS shared credentials file.

cliSteps.command: aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Verify the just-configured CLI profile before it creates any resources.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Arn ends in user/fa-api-gateway-lab-user.
cliSteps.warning: Stop if Account or Arn is not the intended account and user.

verification.title: Verify the lab user policy
verification.instruction: In IAM, open fa-api-gateway-lab-user, choose Permissions, and inspect attached managed policies.
verification.expectedResult: AdministratorAccess is attached to fa-api-gateway-lab-user only.

verification.title: Verify local CLI identity
verification.instruction: Inspect the Arn returned by get-caller-identity.

tasks.title: Create the Lambda execution role and shared backend
tasks.goal: Create the Lambda logging role and fa-api-gateway-lab-hello with a complete Node.js handler that returns the REST API CORS headers.
tasks.whyItMatters: Lambda proxy integrations return Lambda's status, body, and headers directly. The Lambda execution role needs logging permission; API Gateway invocation permission is added later per API.

consoleSteps.title: Create the logging role
consoleSteps.instruction: Open IAM, choose Roles, and choose Create role.

instructions.text: Open IAM, choose Roles, and choose Create role.
Select AWS service, select Lambda, and choose Next.
Select AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole, choose Next, enter fa-api-gateway-lab-lambda-role for Role name, and choose Create role.

consoleSteps.warning: Do not add VPC, database, or broad service permissions; this function only writes logs.

consoleSteps.title: Create and deploy the function
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Lambda, choose Functions, and choose Create function.

instructions.text: Open Lambda, choose Functions, and choose Create function.
Select Author from scratch. Set Function name to fa-api-gateway-lab-hello and Runtime to Node.js 22.x.
Expand Change default execution role, select Use an existing role, select fa-api-gateway-lab-lambda-role, and choose Create function.
On the Code tab, open index.mjs, replace all editor content with the supplied index.mjs block, and choose Deploy.

jsonBlocks.title: index.mjs

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The function becomes Active and deployed code returns statusCode 200, JSON, and the stated CORS headers.
consoleSteps.warning: The origin is deliberately fixed. CORS is not authentication.

cliSteps.explanation: Create a new local fa-api-gateway-lab directory and save the complete Lambda source as fa-api-gateway-lab/index.mjs.
cliSteps.expectedResult: index.mjs exists in the new directory.
cliSteps.warning: The file contains no credentials, token, or API-key value.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-role --role-name fa-api-gateway-lab-lambda-role --assume-role-policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"lambda.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}' --profile fa-api-gateway-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Create the Lambda-trusted role and record Role.Arn as [LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains [LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN].
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name fa-api-gateway-lab-lambda-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole --profile fa-api-gateway-lab
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the Lambda basic logging managed policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes successfully.
cliSteps.warning: Wait briefly for IAM propagation before creating the function.

cliSteps.command: cd fa-api-gateway-lab && zip fa-api-gateway-lab-hello.zip index.mjs
cliSteps.explanation: Package exactly the complete index.mjs file created in this task.
cliSteps.expectedResult: fa-api-gateway-lab-hello.zip exists in fa-api-gateway-lab.
cliSteps.warning: Run this from the parent directory.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda create-function --function-name fa-api-gateway-lab-hello --runtime nodejs22.x --handler index.handler --role [LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN] --zip-file fileb://fa-api-gateway-lab/fa-api-gateway-lab-hello.zip --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [LAMBDA_ROLE_ARN] with the create-role output and record FunctionArn as [LAMBDA_FUNCTION_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes FunctionArn and State Pending or Active.
cliSteps.warning: If role assumption has not propagated, wait and retry rather than changing the trust policy.

verification.title: Verify the handler
verification.instruction: Test the function with {} in the Lambda console, or invoke it after State is Active.
verification.expectedResult: The result has statusCode 200 and Access-Control-Allow-Origin https://example.com.

verification.title: Verify function state
verification.instruction: Run aws lambda get-function --function-name fa-api-gateway-lab-hello --query 'Configuration.State' --output text --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2.

tasks.title: Create Cognito authentication and a test token
tasks.goal: Create fa-api-gateway-lab-users, fa-api-gateway-lab-client without a secret, and api-learner, then obtain an ID token without printing a password in a command.
tasks.whyItMatters: The REST authorizer accepts the user-pool identity token, and the HTTP JWT authorizer validates its issuer and app-client audience.

consoleSteps.title: Create the pool and app client
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Amazon Cognito, choose User pools, then choose Create user pool.

instructions.text: Open Amazon Cognito, choose User pools, then choose Create user pool.
Set User pool name to fa-api-gateway-lab-users. Select Cognito user pool sign-in options and User name. Keep self-registration disabled and complete the wizard.
At the app-client step, set App client name to fa-api-gateway-lab-client and ensure Generate a client secret is off. Create the user pool.
On the pool Overview, record User pool ID as [USER_POOL_ID] and User pool ARN as [USER_POOL_ARN]. Open App clients, select fa-api-gateway-lab-client, and record Client ID as [APP_CLIENT_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The eu-west-2 user pool and public app client exist.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not record a password or JWT in notes or screenshots.

consoleSteps.title: Create a permanent test user
consoleSteps.instruction: In fa-api-gateway-lab-users, choose Users and Create user.

instructions.text: In fa-api-gateway-lab-users, choose Users and Create user.
Set Username to api-learner. Enter a new temporary lab-only password and create the user.
Open api-learner, choose Reset password if needed, and set a new permanent lab-only password.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: api-learner is Enabled and has a permanent password.

cliSteps.command: aws cognito-idp create-user-pool --pool-name fa-api-gateway-lab-users --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create a standard username user pool. Record UserPool.Id as [USER_POOL_ID] and UserPool.Arn as [USER_POOL_ARN].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the pool ID and ARN.
cliSteps.warning: Do not use --username-attributes username.

cliSteps.command: aws cognito-idp create-user-pool-client --user-pool-id [USER_POOL_ID] --client-name fa-api-gateway-lab-client --no-generate-secret --explicit-auth-flows ALLOW_USER_PASSWORD_AUTH ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [USER_POOL_ID] and record UserPoolClient.ClientId as [APP_CLIENT_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The client has a ClientId and no ClientSecret.
cliSteps.warning: This public client is only for the lab.

cliSteps.command: read -s -p 'Temporary lab password: ' TEMP_PASSWORD; echo; aws cognito-idp admin-create-user --user-pool-id [USER_POOL_ID] --username api-learner --temporary-password "$TEMP_PASSWORD" --message-action SUPPRESS --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2; unset TEMP_PASSWORD
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [USER_POOL_ID]. The shell does not echo the temporary password; SUPPRESS prevents email delivery.
cliSteps.expectedResult: api-learner has UserStatus FORCE_CHANGE_PASSWORD.
cliSteps.warning: Use a new lab-only password.

cliSteps.command: read -s -p 'Permanent lab password: ' PERM_PASSWORD; echo; aws cognito-idp admin-set-user-password --user-pool-id [USER_POOL_ID] --username api-learner --password "$PERM_PASSWORD" --permanent --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2; unset PERM_PASSWORD
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [USER_POOL_ID] and establish the permanent password needed for USER_PASSWORD_AUTH.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command completes successfully.
cliSteps.warning: The password is not echoed, but avoid shared terminals.

cliSteps.command: read -s -p 'Permanent lab password: ' PERM_PASSWORD; echo; export ID_TOKEN=$(aws cognito-idp initiate-auth --auth-flow USER_PASSWORD_AUTH --client-id [APP_CLIENT_ID] --auth-parameters USERNAME=api-learner,PASSWORD="$PERM_PASSWORD" --query 'AuthenticationResult.IdToken' --output text --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2); unset PERM_PASSWORD; test -n "$ID_TOKEN" && echo 'ID_TOKEN obtained'
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [APP_CLIENT_ID]. Keep [ID_TOKEN] only in this terminal environment for later requests.
cliSteps.expectedResult: ID_TOKEN obtained is printed; the token itself is not printed.
cliSteps.warning: Close the terminal or unset ID_TOKEN after the lab.

verification.title: Verify recorded identifiers
verification.instruction: Inspect the user-pool Overview and app-client details.
verification.expectedResult: [USER_POOL_ID], [USER_POOL_ARN], and [APP_CLIENT_ID] are recorded from visible fields.

verification.title: Verify token acquisition
verification.instruction: Run test -n "$ID_TOKEN" && echo token-present in the same terminal.

tasks.title: Create the REST API and Lambda proxy integration
tasks.goal: Create fa-api-gateway-lab-rest with GET /hello and integrate it with the shared Lambda function.
tasks.whyItMatters: REST API methods invoke an integration. A Lambda proxy integration passes the request to Lambda and returns the Lambda response to the caller.

consoleSteps.title: Create the Regional REST API and /hello resource

instructions.text: ☐ Enter Beginner REST API lab in Description.
☐ Select Regional in API endpoint type.
☐ Select IPv4 in IP address type.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A Regional REST API contains the /hello resource.
consoleSteps.warning: No VPC is created because this public API invokes a managed Lambda service directly and has no VPC integration in this scope.

consoleSteps.title: Create the GET Lambda proxy method

instructions.text: ☐ Choose OK if prompted to grant API Gateway permission to invoke the function.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: GET /hello has a Lambda proxy integration to fa-api-gateway-lab-hello.
consoleSteps.warning: The Console adds the Lambda resource-based permission when you approve the prompt.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway create-rest-api --name fa-api-gateway-lab-rest --description 'Beginner REST API lab' --endpoint-configuration types=REGIONAL,ipAddressType=ipv4 --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record id as [REST_API_ID] and rootResourceId as [REST_ROOT_RESOURCE_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains a REST API ID and root resource ID.
cliSteps.warning: Use the returned IDs only for this lab API.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway create-resource --rest-api-id [REST_API_ID] --parent-id [REST_ROOT_RESOURCE_ID] --path-part hello --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record id as [REST_HELLO_RESOURCE_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response path is /hello.
cliSteps.warning: Replace both placeholders from the prior command output.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway put-method --rest-api-id [REST_API_ID] --resource-id [REST_HELLO_RESOURCE_ID] --http-method GET --authorization-type NONE --api-key-required --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Create GET /hello and require an API key. Cognito authorization is attached in the next phase.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies GET as the method.
cliSteps.warning: API keys are not authentication or authorization; Cognito is added later.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway put-integration --rest-api-id [REST_API_ID] --resource-id [REST_HELLO_RESOURCE_ID] --http-method GET --type AWS_PROXY --integration-http-method POST --uri arn:aws:apigateway:eu-west-2:lambda:path/2015-03-31/functions/[LAMBDA_FUNCTION_ARN]/invocations --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [LAMBDA_FUNCTION_ARN] with the full Lambda function ARN recorded in Task 2.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies an AWS_PROXY integration.
cliSteps.warning: The integration URI uses the API Gateway Lambda invocation URI format.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda add-permission --function-name fa-api-gateway-lab-hello --statement-id fa-api-gateway-lab-rest-invoke --action lambda:InvokeFunction --principal apigateway.amazonaws.com --source-arn arn:aws:execute-api:eu-west-2:<ACCOUNT_ID>:[REST_API_ID]/*/GET/hello --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the account ID from get-caller-identity and [REST_API_ID] with the REST API ID. The SourceArn restricts invocation to this API method path.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains a Lambda policy statement.
cliSteps.warning: Do not grant apigateway.amazonaws.com unrestricted permission without a SourceArn.

verification.title: Confirm the method integration
verification.instruction: Open GET under /hello and inspect Integration request.
verification.expectedResult: Integration type is Lambda proxy integration and the Lambda function is fa-api-gateway-lab-hello.

verification.title: Confirm Lambda permission scope
verification.instruction: Run aws lambda get-policy --function-name fa-api-gateway-lab-hello --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2.
verification.expectedResult: The policy includes statement ID fa-api-gateway-lab-rest-invoke restricted to the REST API SourceArn.

tasks.title: Secure, deploy, meter, and configure CORS for the REST API
tasks.feature: REST API Cognito authorizer, usage plan, API key, and CORS
tasks.goal: Attach a Cognito authorizer to GET /hello, deploy prod, create a usage plan and generated API key, and retain restrictive CORS headers in the Lambda proxy response.
tasks.whyItMatters: Cognito validates user identity; the API key and usage plan identify a consumer and apply quota/throttle settings. AWS documents that API keys must not be used as authorization. With a Lambda proxy integration, Lambda returns actual-response CORS headers.

consoleSteps.title: Create and attach the REST API Cognito authorizer

instructions.text: ☐ Select eu-west-2 in Cognito user pool Region.
☐ Select fa-api-gateway-lab-users in Cognito user pool.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: GET /hello requires both a valid Cognito token in Authorization and an API key in x-api-key.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not treat the API key as a password, user identity, or authorization control.

consoleSteps.title: Deploy the REST API and record its invoke URL
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The prod stage exists and its invoke URL ends with /prod.
consoleSteps.warning: Redeploy this REST API after method or authorizer changes.

consoleSteps.title: Create the usage plan and generated API key

instructions.text: ☐ Select Create and add new key.
☐ Record the displayed key value only as [REST_API_KEY] in a secure local terminal variable.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The usage plan is associated with REST API stage prod and contains one generated API key.
consoleSteps.warning: API key values are transmitted in headers and can be logged. Do not put the value in source code or screenshots.

consoleSteps.title: Confirm the REST API proxy CORS policy

instructions.text: ☐ Choose Deploy only if you changed the code.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Lambda proxy response supplies restrictive CORS headers for the REST API actual response.
consoleSteps.warning: For Lambda proxy integrations, API Gateway does not generate actual-response CORS headers; the backend must return them.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway create-authorizer --rest-api-id [REST_API_ID] --name fa-api-gateway-lab-rest-cognito --type COGNITO_USER_POOLS --provider-arns [USER_POOL_ARN] --identity-source method.request.header.Authorization --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace [REST_API_ID] and [USER_POOL_ARN]. Record id as [REST_AUTHORIZER_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response type is COGNITO_USER_POOLS.
cliSteps.warning: The user pool and REST API must be in eu-west-2.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway update-method --rest-api-id [REST_API_ID] --resource-id [REST_HELLO_RESOURCE_ID] --http-method GET --patch-operations op=replace,path=/authorizationType,value=COGNITO_USER_POOLS op=replace,path=/authorizerId,value=[REST_AUTHORIZER_ID] --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the Cognito authorizer to GET /hello while retaining the earlier API-key requirement.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The method shows authorizationType COGNITO_USER_POOLS.
cliSteps.warning: Use an identity token in Authorization when no authorization scope is configured.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway create-deployment --rest-api-id [REST_API_ID] --stage-name prod --description 'Initial secure REST API deployment' --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record id as [REST_DEPLOYMENT_ID]. The REST invoke URL is https://[REST_API_ID].execute-api.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/prod.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The deployment response contains stageName prod.
cliSteps.warning: Deploy again after subsequent REST API configuration changes.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway create-usage-plan --name fa-api-gateway-lab-plan --description 'Training plan for one REST API stage' --throttle burstLimit=2,rateLimit=1 --quota limit=20,offset=0,period=DAY --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record id as [USAGE_PLAN_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the throttle and quota configuration.
cliSteps.warning: Usage-plan quotas and throttles are best-effort controls and must not be used as a cost-control guarantee.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway update-usage-plan --usage-plan-id [USAGE_PLAN_ID] --patch-operations op=add,path=/apiStages,value='[REST_API_ID]:prod' --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Associate the REST API prod stage with the usage plan.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response apiStages contains the REST API and prod stage.
cliSteps.warning: Replace both placeholders with values from this lab.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway create-api-key --name fa-api-gateway-lab-key --enabled --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Record id as [REST_API_KEY_ID]. Retrieve the value only when required for local testing.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies an enabled API key.
cliSteps.warning: Do not provide an API-key value yourself; allow API Gateway to generate it.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway create-usage-plan-key --usage-plan-id [USAGE_PLAN_ID] --key-type API_KEY --key-id [REST_API_KEY_ID] --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Associate the generated key with the training usage plan.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains keyType API_KEY.
cliSteps.warning: Association propagation can take a few minutes.

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway create-deployment --rest-api-id [REST_API_ID] --stage-name prod --description 'Deploy Cognito authorization and CORS-capable backend' --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Redeploy the REST API after authorizer configuration. The CORS headers are returned by the Lambda proxy backend code from Task 2.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The prod stage points at the new deployment.
cliSteps.warning: Do not attempt to configure proxy-integration actual-response CORS headers through API Gateway integration responses.

tasks.title: Create the HTTP API and Lambda integration
tasks.goal: Create fa-api-gateway-lab-http, its GET /hello route, a Lambda proxy integration, and a named prod stage.
tasks.whyItMatters: HTTP APIs are a separate API Gateway API type with a simpler feature set, lower-price design, built-in CORS support, and automatic deployment support.

consoleSteps.title: Create the HTTP API and Lambda integration
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The HTTP API contains a GET /hello route backed by the Lambda function and an auto-deploy prod stage.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 create-api --name fa-api-gateway-lab-http --protocol-type HTTP --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 create-integration --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --integration-type AWS_PROXY --integration-uri [LAMBDA_FUNCTION_ARN] --payload-format-version 2.0 --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 create-route --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --route-key 'GET /hello' --target integrations/[HTTP_INTEGRATION_ID] --authorization-type NONE --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2

cliSteps.command: aws lambda add-permission --function-name fa-api-gateway-lab-hello --statement-id fa-api-gateway-lab-http-invoke --action lambda:InvokeFunction --principal apigateway.amazonaws.com --source-arn arn:aws:execute-api:eu-west-2:<ACCOUNT_ID>:[HTTP_API_ID]/*/GET/hello --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> and [HTTP_API_ID]. This statement limits API Gateway invocation to the HTTP API GET /hello route.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 create-stage --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --stage-name prod --auto-deploy --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2

tasks.title: Protect the HTTP API with a Cognito JWT authorizer and restrictive CORS
tasks.feature: HTTP API JWT authorization and CORS
tasks.goal: Create a Cognito JWT authorizer for the HTTP API, attach it to GET /hello, and configure CORS to accept only https://example.com.
tasks.whyItMatters: The HTTP API validates the token issuer and audience before Lambda runs. HTTP API CORS is configured at the API level; API Gateway automatically responds to preflight OPTIONS requests and adds configured CORS headers to integration responses.

consoleSteps.title: Create and attach the JWT authorizer
consoleSteps.expectedResult: GET /hello requires a JWT whose issuer is the training user pool and audience is the training app client.
consoleSteps.warning: Replace only [USER_POOL_ID] and [APP_CLIENT_ID] with values recorded in Task 3.

consoleSteps.title: Configure the HTTP API CORS policy
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The API-level CORS configuration allows only the specified origin and the headers required by this lab.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not use * when you need a precise origin policy. HTTP API CORS configuration overrides CORS headers returned by the backend.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 create-authorizer --name fa-api-gateway-lab-http-jwt --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --authorizer-type JWT --identity-source '$request.header.Authorization' --jwt-configuration Audience=[APP_CLIENT_ID],Issuer=https://cognito-idp.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/[USER_POOL_ID] --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Replace the three placeholders. Record AuthorizerId as [HTTP_AUTHORIZER_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response authorizerType is JWT.
cliSteps.warning: The issuer URL must exactly use the user-pool ID and eu-west-2.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 update-route --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --route-id [HTTP_ROUTE_ID] --authorization-type JWT --authorizer-id [HTTP_AUTHORIZER_ID] --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Attach the JWT authorizer to GET /hello.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The route response has AuthorizationType JWT and the named authorizer ID.
cliSteps.warning: An invalid or absent token is rejected before the Lambda integration runs.

cliSteps.command: aws apigatewayv2 update-api --api-id [HTTP_API_ID] --cors-configuration AllowOrigins=https://example.com,AllowMethods=GET,OPTIONS,AllowHeaders=Authorization,X-Api-Key,Content-Type,MaxAge=300 --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Set API-level CORS. API Gateway responds to eligible preflight requests and adds the configured headers to responses.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The API response includes CorsConfiguration with the supplied origin, methods, headers, and max age.
cliSteps.warning: Do not configure AllowCredentials with a wildcard origin.

tasks.title: Test all security boundaries and review logs
tasks.goal: Observe successful and rejected requests, inspect the Lambda log group created by invocation, and record the difference between REST API and HTTP API features used in this lab.
tasks.whyItMatters: A secure API must reject missing credentials and unexpected browser origins as designed. CloudWatch Logs provide the first troubleshooting location for backend Lambda execution.

consoleSteps.title: Test successful and rejected API calls

cliSteps.command: aws apigateway get-api-key --api-key [REST_API_KEY_ID] --include-value --query value --output text --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2

cliSteps.expectedResult: The command prints the key value.
cliSteps.warning: Do not redirect the key to a shared file or paste it into source code.

cliSteps.command: curl -i -H "Authorization: [ID_TOKEN]" -H "x-api-key: [REST_API_KEY]" https://[REST_API_ID].execute-api.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/prod/hello
cliSteps.explanation: Invoke the protected REST API with both required controls.
cliSteps.expectedResult: HTTP 200 with the Lambda JSON response and REST proxy CORS headers.
cliSteps.warning: Replace terminal-only token and key placeholders; do not save the command in shell history if it contains real values.

cliSteps.command: curl -i -H "Authorization: [ID_TOKEN]" https://[HTTP_API_ID].execute-api.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/prod/hello
cliSteps.explanation: Invoke the HTTP API with a valid JWT.
cliSteps.expectedResult: HTTP 200 with the Lambda JSON response and HTTP API CORS headers when an Origin header is supplied.
cliSteps.warning: The HTTP API has no REST API usage-plan or API-key requirement.

cliSteps.command: curl -i -X OPTIONS -H "Origin: https://not-example.com" -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: GET" https://[HTTP_API_ID].execute-api.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/prod/hello
cliSteps.explanation: Test an origin that is not in the configured HTTP API CORS allow list.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response does not allow https://not-example.com as Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
cliSteps.warning: A non-browser curl request is not blocked by CORS; browsers enforce the CORS policy.

cliSteps.command: aws logs describe-log-groups --log-group-name-prefix /aws/lambda/fa-api-gateway-lab-hello --profile fa-api-gateway-lab --region eu-west-2

cliSteps.expectedResult: The output contains /aws/lambda/fa-api-gateway-lab-hello.
cliSteps.warning: This command only reads log-group metadata.

verification.title: State the security division of responsibility
verification.instruction: Explain the REST API controls and the HTTP API controls used here.
verification.expectedResult: REST API: Cognito authorizer validates identity and API key/usage plan applies consumer quota and throttling; HTTP API: Cognito JWT authorizer validates issuer and audience; both: Lambda integration provides the backend response; CORS controls browser cross-origin access rather than API authentication.

verification.title: Confirm no VPC resources were needed
verification.expectedResult: No VPC, subnet, route table, security group, NAT gateway, or internet gateway was created because neither API uses a VPC integration in this requested scope.

warnings.cost: API Gateway, Lambda, Amazon Cognito, and CloudWatch Logs can incur charges depending on account usage and Free Tier eligibility. Usage plans do not guarantee spend control. Delete the resources promptly after testing.
warnings.safety: No VPC, subnet, security group, NAT gateway, internet gateway, database, or public compute instance is required for this managed Lambda integration lab. The REST API requires Cognito plus an API key. The HTTP API requires a Cognito JWT. CORS is configured for https://example.com and is not an authentication mechanism.
warnings.credentials: Never create root access keys. Never place access-key secrets, passwords, API-key values, JWTs, or session tokens in source code, user data, screenshots, notes, command history, or shared terminals. Delete the local fa-api-gateway-lab AWS CLI profile manually after deleting its IAM access key.
warnings.region: Use Europe (London), eu-west-2, for every regional resource and CLI command. IAM commands intentionally omit --region because IAM is global.
